title: “And how, monks, is a monk called a ‘noble one’? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful,…
content: “And how, monks, is a monk called a ‘noble one’? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is called a noble one.”

title: “Monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye and saw beings with little dust in their…
content: “Monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye and saw beings with little dust in their eyes and with much dust in their eyes, with sharp faculties and with dull faculties, with good dispositions and with bad dispositions, some easy to teach and some hard to teach, and a few who saw the danger in rebirth in another world and the danger of faulty actions. Just as in a blue lotus pond, a red lotus pond, or a white lotus pond, some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, do not rise above the water, and are nourished underwater; some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, and reach the water’s surface; some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, rise up above the water and are not wetted by the water.”

title: - “Venerable sir, I do not understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One regarding the purpose of purity of virtue.” - “Monk, if you…
content: - “Venerable sir, I do not understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One regarding the purpose of purity of virtue.” - “Monk, if you do not understand the Dhamma I have taught regarding the purpose of purity of virtue, then how, monk, do you understand the Dhamma I have taught?” - “Venerable sir, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One as greed and the removal of greed.” - “Good, good, monk! Good, monk! You understand the Dhamma taught by me as greed and the removal of greed. It is for the purpose of greed and the removal of greed, monk, that the Dhamma is taught by me. What do you think, monk: Is the eye permanent or impermanent?” - “Impermanent, venerable sir.” - “The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … Is the mind permanent or impermanent?” - “Impermanent, venerable sir.” - “What is impermanent — is that suffering or happiness?” - “Suffering, venerable sir.” - “What is impermanent, suffering, subject to change — is it fitting to regard it as: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” - “No, venerable sir.” - “Seeing thus, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye … disenchanted with the mind … Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate … He knows: ‘… there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: The hunter set his trap and snare, The wise deer does not approach, Having eaten the crops, we go our way, Leaving the trapper to…
content:
The hunter set his trap and snare,
The wise deer does not approach,
Having eaten the crops, we go our way,
Leaving the trapper to lament.

title: “Monks, there are these three things. What three? Sensual thought, ill-will thought, harmful thought. Monks, these are the three things. To abandon these three things,…
content: “Monks, there are these three things. What three? Sensual thought, ill-will thought, harmful thought. Monks, these are the three things. To abandon these three things, three things should be developed. What three? To abandon sensual thought, the thought of renunciation should be developed. To abandon ill-will thought, the thought of non-ill-will should be developed. To abandon harmful thought, the thought of harmlessness should be developed. To abandon those three things, monks, these three things should be developed.”

title: “Suppose, Rādha, young boys or girls are playing with sandcastles. As long as their desire, lust, love, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles are…
content: “Suppose, Rādha, young boys or girls are playing with sandcastles. As long as their desire, lust, love, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles are not fully abandoned, they still cling to them, delight in them, treasure them, and are attached to them. But when their desire, lust, love, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles are fully abandoned, then they smash them, scatter them, demolish them with their hands and feet and no longer play with them. So too, Rādha, you should smash, scatter, demolish form and not play with it, being intent on the destruction of craving for form. The destruction of craving, Rādha, is Nibbāna.”

title: “What benefit could there be, Aggivessana? Prince Jayasenna, living amidst sensual pleasures, enjoying sensual pleasures, being consumed by sensual thoughts, burned by the fever of…
content: “What benefit could there be, Aggivessana? Prince Jayasenna, living amidst sensual pleasures, enjoying sensual pleasures, being consumed by sensual thoughts, burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, ardently pursuing sensual pleasures — could he know, see, or attain the state that can only be known, seen, attained, or realized through seclusion from sensual pleasures? Such a thing does not occur.”

title: “‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day,…
content: “‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day, I too abandon unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. In this factor, I follow the arahants and will observe the uposatha day.’”

title: “Why laughter, why joy, When the world is always burning? Shrouded in darkness, Why do you not seek a light?” “Behold this painted image, This…
content:
“Why laughter, why joy,
When the world is always burning?
Shrouded in darkness,
Why do you not seek a light?”

“Behold this painted image,
This heap of wounds,
Diseased, full of many thoughts,
Of nothing stable or lasting.”

“This form is worn out,
A nest of diseases, fragile;
This putrid mass breaks apart —
Death is the end of life.”

“Like a gourd in autumn,
Abandoned and cast away,
Seeing these bleached bones,
What pleasure can there be?”

title: “Monks, abandon one thing. I guarantee you no further rebirth. What one thing? Greed, monks, is that one thing. Abandon it! I guarantee you no…
content:
“Monks, abandon one thing. I guarantee you no further rebirth. What one thing? Greed, monks, is that one thing. Abandon it! I guarantee you no further rebirth.” The Blessed One spoke this meaning. Here it is said:

With greed, beings,
Infatuated, go to a bad destination.
But the meditator, with right knowledge,
Abandons that greed.
Having abandoned it, he never
Returns to this world again.
